_source: safeguarding-questions.json from the client (2026-11-25): six sections of ten questions, every answer on a 0 to 3 scale.

questions.text: I worry that I will not be able to join online sessions successfully.
I feel anxious or unsure when using my camera, microphone, speakers or meeting settings.
I avoid using chat, reactions, polls, breakout rooms or shared screens because I am unsure how they work.
I find it difficult to log in to the LMS, find resources, access recordings or complete online activities.
I feel anxious when uploading assignments, evidence, files or forms online.
I find it difficult to download, edit, save, rename or upload documents correctly.
I worry that I will click the wrong button, lose my work, submit the wrong file or break something online.
I feel overwhelmed by having to use multiple systems, passwords, links or apps.
I do not always have reliable access to a suitable device, internet connection or quiet space for online learning.
Technology issues or technology anxiety affect my attendance, participation or assignment submission.
I find it difficult to read small text on slides, PDFs, websites, forms or the LMS.
I find it difficult to see shared screens, diagrams, charts or visual content during online sessions.
I experience eye strain, headaches, blurred vision or tiredness when using screens for learning.
I would benefit from larger text, zoomed documents, high contrast, clear layouts or accessible PDFs.
I use, or may benefit from, screen reader, magnification, text-to-speech or other visual accessibility tools.
I find it difficult to hear tutors, peers or employers clearly during online sessions.
Background noise, unclear sound, poor microphones or several people speaking at once make sessions difficult.
I would benefit from captions, transcripts, recordings or written summaries of sessions.
I use, or may benefit from, hearing aids, assistive listening tools or hearing-related support.
Vision or hearing difficulties affect my attendance, participation, understanding or assignment progress.
I read more slowly than other people when reading learning materials, slides, forms or instructions.
I feel tired, lose focus, or get headaches when reading for a long time.
I need to read the same information more than once before I understand it.
I lose my place, skip lines, or misread words when reading longer text.
I make spelling mistakes, even with words I use regularly.
I know what I want to say, but I find it difficult to write it clearly.
I need extra time to understand written instructions, assignment briefs or forms.
I make mistakes when copying information from slides, screens, documents or notes.
I find it difficult to remember or follow instructions with several steps.
I have previously received support for reading, writing, spelling, processing speed or dyslexia.
I find it difficult to stay focused during online sessions, lessons, meetings or long explanations.
I miss important information because my attention drifts, even when I am trying to listen.
I am easily distracted by notifications, noise, people, emails or unrelated thoughts.
I find it difficult to organise tasks, notes, files, learning materials or priorities.
I struggle to plan my time or keep track of deadlines.
I forget appointments, commitments, tasks, passwords or things I need for learning.
I delay starting assignments or tasks that require sustained thinking.
I start tasks but move on to something else before finishing them.
I feel restless, fidgety, impatient, or find it difficult to sit still or wait my turn.
These attention, organisation or restlessness difficulties affect my learning, work or assignment progress.
I feel anxious before giving a presentation or speaking in front of others.
I worry that I will forget my words, make mistakes, or not explain myself clearly during presentations.
I feel anxious when asked to speak on microphone during online sessions.
I feel uncomfortable or anxious when asked to turn my camera on during online sessions.
I avoid answering questions or contributing in live sessions, even when I know the answer.
I feel anxious in breakout rooms, group discussions or small group activities.
I worry that other learners, tutors or employers will judge me negatively when I speak.
I avoid asking questions because I do not want to appear confused or draw attention to myself.
I feel anxious about professional discussions, interviews, verbal assessments or EPA-style conversations.
Anxiety about speaking or interacting affects my participation, confidence or ability to show what I know.
I have felt low, down, or emotionally unsettled in a way that affects my learning.
I have felt discouraged or less hopeful about my progress or future.
I have lost interest or motivation in learning, work, or activities I usually care about.
I feel tired, drained, or low in energy during learning or work.
My sleep quality or sleep routine affects my ability to learn or complete tasks.
My mood, stress, or energy levels make it difficult to concentrate.
My wellbeing has made it difficult to attend live sessions or arrive prepared.
My wellbeing has made it difficult to start, continue, or complete assignments.
I feel overwhelmed by learning, work, or personal responsibilities.
I would benefit from wellbeing support, extra check-ins, or a temporary learning support plan.
